title: Woodward's reserpine: the Diels–Alder reaction
subtitle: Benzoquinone and methyl vinylacrylate build the cis-fused E-ring precursor

reactants.caption: p-benzoquinone + methyl (E)-penta-2,4-dienoate (methyl vinylacrylate)
reactants.learnerPrompt: Woodward's first step: a Diels–Alder reaction. Draw the cycloaddition between the diene and one C=C of the quinone.
hintTiers: The diene is the four-carbon chain with two C=C bonds; the quinone is the dienophile. Which bond of the quinone is the dienophile: a C=C or a C=O?

One C=C of the quinone, pulled electron-poor by both its C=O groups, reacts. The two ends of the diene (the CH₂ and the CH next to the ester) each make a new σ bond to one carbon of that C=C, and a new C=C appears in the middle of the diene. Three arrows, one step.

Arrow 1: the diene's CH₂=CH π bond → a new σ bond from the CH₂ to one quinone alkene carbon. Arrow 2: the other diene π bond → a π bond between the two middle diene carbons. Arrow 3: the quinone C=C π bond → a new σ bond from its other carbon to the diene carbon next to the ester.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: The quinone C=O bonds take no part. The C=C between the two carbonyls is the dienophile: both C=O groups pull electrons out of it, making it very electron-poor.
Only the two end carbons of the diene make new σ bonds. The middle two end up joined by the new C=C.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right: the CH₂ end of the diene bonds to a quinone alkene carbon. Finish the ring of moving electrons: two more arrows in the same step.

adduct.caption: the cis-fused adduct: the ester-bearing cyclohexene is the future E ring of reserpine

steps.explanationAfterStep: A [4+2] cycloaddition in one concerted step: two new C–C σ bonds and a new C=C, through a six-membered ring of moving electrons. The quinone adds through its endo face, so the two new ring-fusion hydrogens and the hydrogen next to the ester end up on the same face: a cis-fused ring system with three stereocentres set in one step. The app does not check stereochemistry yet.

mechanismSummary: Methyl (E)-penta-2,4-dienoate adds to one C=C of p-benzoquinone in a Diels–Alder reaction: three arrows, one step, two new C–C bonds. Endo addition gives a cis-fused bicyclic adduct in which the two ring-fusion hydrogens and the hydrogen next to the ester all lie on one face. Those three stereocentres become three of the five stereocentres of reserpine's E ring; Woodward used the rigid, folded shape of the cis-fused rings to control every later stereocentre (stereochemistry is explained here, not yet checked by the app).
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 34 (pericyclic reactions 1: cycloadditions)
R. B. Woodward, F. E. Bader, H. Bickel, A. J. Frey and R. W. Kierstead, The total synthesis of reserpine, J. Am. Chem. Soc., 1956, 78, 2023–2025 and 2657; Tetrahedron, 1958, 2, 1–57
